summary: The patch changes SSTable.delete (SSTable.java:109-123) to capture each component's lastModified, sort ascending, and delete oldest first, so the max timestamp that LogFile.verifyRecord checks survives partial deletes. The DATA-first and SUMMARY-last special cases are removed. Checklist applied: resources.md (bundle), with emphasis on items 7, 11, 12 and 21 (resource and IO failure paths), item 1 (ordering parity), and the observability and mixed-version lens rules. Nothing in the patch changes a serialized form, the REMOVE record format, or any metric, so mixed-version and metric checks were clean. The worktree was read directly (SSTable.java, FileUtils.java, LogFile.java, LogRecord.java, LogTransaction.java). Not reviewed: nothing. Tests were not run.

findings.rule: resources.md 11/12: failed deletion must surface and be retried, not be swallowed; error handling must not swallow disk failure
findings.problem: The new loop calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns File.delete()'s boolean and discards it (FileUtils.java:545-549). The old code used FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY, which throws FSWriteError. On a real failure (EACCES, EIO, or a file held open on Windows), SSTable.delete now returns true with no log line. SSTableTidier (LogTransaction.java:401-407) therefore sees success, removes the transaction log, and decrements totalDiskSpaceUsed (around LogTransaction.java:415). The old catch-and-retry path via failedDeletions never runs, so the leftover component stays on disk as an orphan with no error reported.
findings.fix: In the loop, call FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) instead of FileUtils.delete(...). This keeps the new sort order and restores the FSWriteError and retry behaviour for every component, including SUMMARY.

findings.rule: Ordering invariant from the ticket (delete in last-modified order so the REMOVE record timestamp still matches on restart)
findings.problem: On the SSTableTidier path, LogTransaction deletes the DATA file directly (line 396, delete(datafile)) before calling the newly sorted SSTable.delete at line 401. DATA is therefore removed outside the mtime ordering. If Data.db is the most recently modified component, a crash after it is removed but before the rest leaves a max timestamp that differs from the REMOVE record. LogFile.verifyRecord (LogFile.java:258-272) then reports 'Unexpected files detected' and the node refuses to start. This needs DATA to be the newest file, which is unusual for the usual write order, so confidence is low.
findings.fix: Drop the separate DATA pre-delete at line 395-396 and let SSTable.delete remove DATA in timestamp order too. If the DATA pre-delete is kept for the retry-tracking reason, document that the timestamp guarantee does not hold for DATA on this path.
